chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr, the two sons of Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When one is convinced that he has increased in his prescribed prayer, he should not rely upon it, and he should re-commence his prayer with a fresh commencement, provided that he was convinced with certainty.

key_terms.لَمْ يَعْتَدَّ بِهَا: he did not rely upon it / it was not counted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one is certain they added an extra unit to their prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'certainty overriding doubt' (yaqin al-yaqin) in Shia jurisprudence, ruling that if a worshipper is absolutely certain they added an extra rak'ah to an obligatory prayer, the entire prayer is invalidated and must be restarted from the beginning. This contrasts with cases of mere doubt, where the default assumption of correctness usually applies, highlighting the rigorous standards for certainty in ritual validity. The narration, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah and Bukayr ibn A'yan, underscores the importance of precise self-awareness during worship.
